observations: Photo 0: a dusty black alternator unit viewed from the rear, showing a label with a visible 'Valeo' logo and a part-number sticker whose digits are too small/blurred to read.
Photo 0: regulator brush box and B+ terminal stud visible, consistent with a standard automotive alternator.
Photo 1: close-up of the alternator's side vents showing copper stator windings; a visible horizontal seam/line runs across the casing where the front and rear housings join.
Photo 2: front view showing the pulley (multi-rib type) and the same casing seam line continuing around the housing.
General surface dust, grime and light corrosion visible on all casing surfaces; no obvious cracks, oil leakage, or burn marks seen.
No video, bench-test rig, voltmeter reading, or sound clip is provided to support the 'tested and working, no knock' claims.
No photo shows the full legible part-number sticker that would confirm the specific Mercedes-Benz M278 '439741' reference claimed in the text.

risks.risk: Alternator may not actually charge or may have worn brushes/bearings despite the 'tested and working' claim.
risks.proof: A video clip of the alternator spinning (e.g., on a bench test rig or drill-spin test) with a voltmeter showing output voltage.

risks.risk: Internal wear (slip rings, bearings, diode pack) not visible from exterior photos.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the slip rings/brushes and a bearing spin-free rotation check.

risks.risk: Part number and fitment for Mercedes-Benz M278 cannot be confirmed, so it could be a mismatched or incompatible unit.
risks.proof: A clear, legible photo of the full label including the part number '439741' and OEM stamping.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic/unconfirmed-fitment alternator, not as verified M278 OEM part

risks.risk: Visible seam line across the housing could indicate prior disassembly/repair inconsistent with the 'never opened' claim.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the seam area and any screw/bolt heads for tamper evidence.

risks.risk: Import/origin claim ('direct from Belgium') cannot be verified and may affect buyer trust in condition grading (Tokunbo standard).
risks.proof: Photo of shipping carton, import paperwork, or container manifest.
risks.if_unproven: priced as standard used/Tokunbo import without premium for verified low-mileage European origin

proof_requests: A clear close-up photo of the full label showing the legible part number matching '439741' and Valeo OEM markings.
A video clip of the alternator being spun (hand drill or bench rig) with a multimeter showing voltage output.
Close-up photos of the slip rings, brushes, and bearing for wear assessment.
A photo of the casing seam area close enough to check for tamper marks or re-sealant residue.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a Valeo-branded automotive alternator (brand legible in photo 0), but all performance and fitment claims (tested, working, no knock, low mileage, specific M278 part number) are unverifiable from the photos, so it must be priced at worst case as an unverified used alternator for a Mercedes-Benz, with the Mercedes-specific comparable as the floor and a higher-value imported alternator as the ceiling given the M278's complexity.
